teenKit.tldr: Your brain hogs 20% of your body's energy despite weighing only 2%, and the chemical exhaust from powering your thoughts slowly rusts your neurons from the inside out.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how intense mental effort creates cellular damage bridges the gap between how we think, why we age, and how neurodegenerative diseases take root.
keyTakeaways: The brain accounts for just 2% of body weight but burns a massive 20% of total systemic oxygen and energy.
Astrocytes act as metabolic delivery trucks, shuttling lactate fuel to hard-working neurons to keep them firing.
The cellular exhaust from intense neural activity causes oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation, literally rusting brain tissue over time.

vocab.meaning: A cellular delivery system discovered in 1994 where support cells pump lactate fuel directly into firing neurons.
The microscopic gap between neurons where chemical messages like glutamate are passed to keep signals moving.
The primary chemical messenger in the central nervous system that opens ion channels to pass electrical signals along.
A destructive chain reaction where reactive oxygen molecules attack fats in cell membranes, causing cellular rust and decay.
